title: ACCESS='DIRECT' with RECL — random-access fixed-length records; record number indexes from 1
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE WRITE_REC(UNIT, RECNUM, X)
C     Direct-access I/O. The file is a flat array of RECL-byte
C     records. RECNUM=1 is the FIRST record (Fortran 1-based);
C     RECNUM=N writes the Nth record. A Java RandomAccessFile.seek
C     is 0-based and counts bytes -- the translation needs offset =
C     (RECNUM - 1) * RECL. Off-by-one bugs here have shipped to
C     production.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER UNIT, RECNUM
      REAL    X(80)
      WRITE (UNIT, REC=RECNUM) X
      END
notes: ACCESS='DIRECT' is the IBM batch-job standard for VSAM-like flat files. The rewrite must (a) compute the byte offset correctly, (b) preserve the RECL contract (record length in bytes, possibly with vendor 'word' multipliers), and (c) ensure 1-based REC= translates to 0-based seek correctly.
